starting_points.name: Xcode iOS App template
starting_points.when: Creating a new native iOS/iPadOS SwiftUI application in a new destination; requires macOS, compatible Xcode, iOS platform support and access to its project wizard.
steps: Record product name, organization/bundle identity, minimum OS, supported devices and signing owner; use a source workspace outside synchronized storage.
In Xcode choose File > New > Project, use Choose Template if offered, select iOS and the App template. Select SwiftUI and Swift where the template offers these options.

Set the product and organization identifier. Choose storage deliberately: enable SwiftData only when required and compatible with the deployment target; record the choice. Select a signing team only when the relevant account is available.

Choose the testing option that provides Swift Testing unit tests and XCTest UI tests; retain established XCTest choices when required. If this template/version omits testing options, add the targets using the follow-up template workflow.

Create/save into a new destination, inspect the generated project, sources and assets, and share the app scheme for CI. Record the actual Xcode version, template, options and generated baseline before editing application code.
notes: This is an official IDE template workflow; xcodebuild builds and tests existing projects and is not an iOS app initializer. swift package init creates a Swift package, not the Xcode iOS App project required here.

If the agent cannot access Xcode's wizard, report that prerequisite and request the template-generated project or an operator handoff. Do not silently substitute hand-written project files or an unreviewed third-party generator.

For an existing app, open and inspect its project/workspace, targets and schemes; do not rerun new-project creation over it. Compare against a separate disposable template project only when investigating missing defaults.

follow_up_generators.name: Xcode test target and test file templates
follow_up_generators.when: The app needs an additional test bundle or test file; inspect existing targets first.
notes: Use File > New > Target, filter for Test, and choose Unit Testing Bundle or UI Testing Bundle; configure the intended app target and finish. Add the resulting targets to the relevant scheme/test plan.
For a test file, use File > New > New File From Template and select Swift Testing Unit Test or XCTest Unit Test, assigning it to the intended test target.
Swift Testing and XCTest tests can coexist in a target; use XCTest/XCUIAutomation for UI tests. Do not recreate existing test bundles merely to add Swift Testing.

follow_up_generators.name: Project and destination discovery before command-line verification
follow_up_generators.when: After the generated project exists and full Xcode with an appropriate simulator runtime is selected; substitute discovered values for every placeholder.

commands.purpose: Verify that the selected developer directory belongs to the required Xcode installation.
Discover the generated targets and schemes; use -workspace for a workspace-owned app.
Discover a supported installed simulator destination after choosing the actual scheme.
Build and run the app's selected unit/UI tests and retain results; requires discovered targets and a simulator.

notes: These commands inspect/build/test the generated app; they do not generate an app. Replace -project with -workspace consistently if that is the actual build owner.
Apple's command-line FAQ is archived: check the selected Xcode's local help for supported flags. Device signing, archives and App Store publication require their separate project release workflow.

preserve: Keep the generated Xcode project configuration, app entry point, asset catalog and selected test targets; document deliberate changes from the recorded template baseline.
Preserve shared schemes, test plans, required build settings, deployment targets and the app's dependency resolution policy; do not replace them with a minimal handwritten project skeleton.

Inspect repository ignore coverage separately: an IDE template is not evidence that .DS_Store, DerivedData, build outputs or personal xcuserdata cannot be staged. Preserve distributable source/assets and shared configuration.
verification: Record template provenance and Xcode version; inspect the actual generated target membership, bundle ID, storage choice and signing configuration.
Confirm the shared app scheme includes the intended test targets, discover a simulator destination and run tests with retained results before claiming the baseline works.

Review Git's candidate file set and ignore behavior without modifying an existing user's index; ensure local caches and personal IDE state are excluded while project configuration and assets remain included.
A simulator pass does not prove device capabilities, signing, accessibility or release readiness. Those require the profile's device and distribution checks.

integration_steps: Record minimum iOS/iPadOS versions, supported devices, capabilities, API schema and signing owner in the project documentation; confirm these choices against the generated baseline.

Pin package resolution and use only dependencies justified by a requirement. Separate SwiftUI views, observable presentation state, repositories and API DTOs; add migration fixtures, versioned network fixtures and a fake API for tests.
Run simulator checks and CI with the discovered shared scheme and actual destination. Verify representative physical devices, offline/reconnect, permissions, VoiceOver and large text.

Have the account owner establish team, bundle ID, capabilities and signing access. Follow the authorized release workflow to produce a signed archive and verify a TestFlight install; retain result bundles and release evidence. An archive is not publication.
